title: KK - 64737 Gårdsveien 1, tilbygg
description: Kristiansund kommune v/ Eiendomsdrift skal lage et tilbygg til bolig i Gårdsveien 1. Tilbygget består av to soverom og en stue. Det skal dessuten skiftes vinduer og bordkledning på en vegg, samt skifte ut noen vindskibord. Denne anskaffelsen gjelder oppsetting av tilbygget, nødvendig grunnarbeid, utskifting av vinduer og en balkongdør, og annet bygningsmessige arbeider, samt arbeid innen tekniske fagområder i denne sammenheng. Bygget ble oppført rundt år 2004. Kristiansund kommune vil bestille rammeavtaleaktører på tekniske fag som vil bli kontrahert for seg. Dette gjelder Malerarbeider, gulvbelegg, Elektro, ventilasjon og evt. rør og sanitær. Det forventes at tømrerfaget tar med seg nødvendige underentreprenører i sitt tilbud som: · Grunnentreprenør · Murer- Støping såle/grunnmur/plate. · Blikkenslager ved behov · Evt andre fag for komplett leveranse. Tømrerfaget/tilbyder tar det overordnede koordineringsansvaret under utførelsesarbeidene, også opp mot de tekniske fagene, og dette skal være inkludert i tilbudet. Tiltakene skal gjennomføres samtidig som beboerne bor i boligen, noe som stiller særskilte krav til planlegging, koordinering, avgrensing av arbeidsområder, renhold og støyhåndtering. Entreprenør må regne med tett dialog med byggherre for å ivareta HMS og logistikk gjennom hele prosjektet.

title: Netherlands – Construction work – Partnerselectie EHAD-terrein Helmond
description: De gemeente, woCom en Woonpartners zijn voor het EHAD-terrein op zoek naar een gebiedsontwikkelaar. Dat wil zeggen een partij, die de complexiteit van de opgave overziet, de ambities voor het EHAD-terrein omarmt en deelt, ervaring heeft met soortgelijke opgaven, langjarig commitment toont en zich hiermee ook langjarig als samenwerkingspartner wil binden aan de opgave. Op basis hiervan hebben de gemeente en de woningcorporaties samengevat het volgende ultieme doel geformuleerd voor deze partnerselectieprocedure: “Het selecteren van een gebiedsontwikkelaar, die voor het EHAD-terrein maximale invulling geeft aan de vijf thema’s uit de Visie Stationskwartier Helmond en zich langjarig committeert aan het gebied in een samenwerking met de gemeente Helmond, woCom en Woonpartners.” De totale bruto vloeroppervlakte van de woonfuncties mag niet meer bedragen dan 50.000 m2 en in aantal maximaal 520 woningen. Het aantal vierkante meters aan niet-woonfuncties (exclusief parkeren) mag niet meer bedragen dan 20.750 m2, als volgt verdeeld: • 16.000 m2 bruto vloeroppervlakte voor bedrijven in de milieucategorie I en II. (definitie passend in/naast/bij woningen); • 3.000 m2 bruto vloeroppervlak voor maatschappelijk (geen zeer kwetsbare groepen); • 1.500 m2 bruto vloeroppervlak voor detailhandel (maximaal 250 m2 bruto vloeroppervlak voor een supermarkt); • 750 m2 bruto vloeroppervlak voor horeca I in minstens twee gebouwen. Het bewoners- en bezoekers parkeren voor alle woningen en alle overige niet-woonfuncties is voorzien in de op het EHAD-terrein te realiseren parkeerhub.

buyer: Gemeente Delft (en de aan de gemeente Delft gelieerde ondernemingen)
title: Netherlands – Engineering design services for the construction of civil engineering works – Ingenieursdiensten Fietsecoduct A13 Gemeente Delft
description: De opdracht betreft het uitvoeren van ingenieurs- en adviesdiensten voor de voorbereiding en uitwerking van het Fietsecoduct A13. De werkzaamheden omvatten onder meer het herijken van het Programma van Eisen en de projectrandvoorwaarden, het uitwerken van het Voorlopig Ontwerp en de daarvoor benodigde onderzoeken en adviezen. De initiële opdracht omvat fase 1 en 2. De vervolgfasen voor het Definitief Ontwerp, de contract- en aanbestedingsdocumenten en de begeleiding van de aanbesteding voor de realisatie kunnen als opties worden opgedragen. De opdracht wordt uitgevoerd in samenwerking met de gemeenten Delft en Pijnacker-Nootdorp, Rijkswaterstaat en overige relevante stakeholders. De opdracht omvat ingenieurs- en adviesdiensten voor het Fietsecoduct A13 en wordt gefaseerd uitgevoerd. De initiële opdracht bestaat uit fase 1 (herijking van het Programma van Eisen en de projectrandvoorwaarden) en fase 2 (uitwerking van het Voorlopig Ontwerp). Daarnaast omvat de aanbesteding mogelijke vervolgfasen: fase 3 (Definitief Ontwerp), fase 4 (opstellen van contract- en aanbestedingsdocumenten) en fase 5 (begeleiding van de aanbesteding voor de realisatie). De opdracht omvat onder meer ontwerp- en advieswerkzaamheden, technische en specialistische onderzoeken, kostenramingen, risicobeheersing, vergunningen en afstemming met Rijkswaterstaat en andere stakeholders. De omvang van de werkzaamheden is nader uitgewerkt in de aanbestedingsleidraad en de bijbehorende bijlagen. Uitsluitend fase 1 en fase 2 worden bij aanvang opgedragen. Opdrachtverlening voor de vervolgfasen is optioneel en afhankelijk van afzonderlijke besluitvorming door de opdrachtgevers.

description: The Minister for Defence (the “Contracting Authority”) is seeking responses from economic operators (“Candidates”) through this Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ) for the purchase of a Multi Modal ROV to the Department of Defence, Ireland for use by the Irish Defence Forces. The requirement exists for the supply of up to 3 units. It is intended that the purchase arising from this competition shall be delivered DAP (Incoterms) Naval Base, Haulbowline, Co. Cork, Ireland. In summary, The Defence Forces wishes to procure up to three (3) multi-function, battery powered ROV’s primarily designed for Maritime Explosive Ordnance Disposal but adaptable for use in theatres such as Search and Recovery (SAR), Mine Counter measures (MCM), and Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP). An option to purchase a third unit will be retained by contracting authority. Launching and recovering must be possible with a 2-man team from land and small boats. Ease of handling and deployment and a user-focused HMI should be to the forefront of tender submissions. Operational depth ≥300m. Further details of the requirements can be found at Appendix 1.

buyer: LHC Procurement Group for the Scottish Procurement Alliance (SPA)
title: Refurbishment and Modernisation (RM4S) - Scotland Framework Agreement
description: LHC Procurement Group Limited (LHCPG) is procuring the Refurbishment and Modernisation Scotland Framework Agreement (RM4S) on behalf of the Scottish Procurement Alliance (SPA). LHCPG is acting as the Contracting Authority and central purchasing body for this procurement. The Framework is being procured solely for use in Scotland and will provide eligible public sector organisations with a compliant and flexible route for the delivery of refurbishment, improvement, repair, maintenance and modernisation works, goods and associated services across residential and non-residential buildings. The procurement is being conducted using the Open Procedure in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 and the Procurement Regulations 2024. When awarding Call-Off Contracts, eligible Clients and Partners must also comply with the Framework Agreement, the applicable Call-Off procedure and any other procurement legislation applicable to them. RM4S builds upon the existing Refurbishment and Modernisation Framework and has been developed following market engagement with suppliers and public sector organisations. Feedback received through that engagement has informed the scope, Workstreams, Lot structure, value bands and regional arrangements. The Framework comprises the following Workstreams and Lots: Painting and Decorating Electrical Works, from zero to 500k Electrical Works, 500k and above Kitchens and Bathrooms, from zero to 500k Kitchens and Bathrooms, 500k to 2m Kitchens and Bathrooms, 2m and above Aids and Adaptations Damp and Mould Remediation Environmental and External Works, External Works Environmental and External Works, Grounds Maintenance Stoneworks Reactive Repairs and Maintenance Multi-Disciplinary Works, from zero to 750k Multi-Disciplinary Works, 750k to 2.5m Multi-Disciplinary Works, 2.5m and above Kitchens (Supply only) The scope may include planned and reactive maintenance, refurbishment and improvement programmes, component replacement, compliance-led works, accessibility adaptations, environmental and external works, property modernisation and wider asset management and investment programmes. Each Lot is divided into five regional areas covering North Eastern Scotland, Highlands and Islands, Eastern Scotland, West Central Scotland and Southern Scotland. Bidders may apply for one or more Lots and regional areas in accordance with the Procurement Documents. Subject to there being sufficient Qualifying Bidders, LHCPG will appoint no more than 10 Appointed Companies for each Lot and regional area. Where a Micro and Small Enterprise Reserved Allocation applies, it forms part of, and is not additional to, the maximum of 10 appointments. The Framework will not operate a reserve list and no additional or replacement Bidders may be appointed during the Framework Term. The Framework is structured to support participation from organisations of different sizes and capabilities through its Workstreams, value bands, regional areas and applicable Micro and Small Enterprise Reserved Allocations. All Bidders will remain subject to the same published qualification, compliance, quality, evaluation and appointment requirements. RM4S is intended to support the delivery of high-quality and compliant solutions, sustainable supply chains, environmental improvement, social value, community benefits, Fair Work and proportionate innovation. Detailed technical requirements, eligibility provisions, award criteria, appointment methodology and Call-Off procedures are set out in the Procurement Documents.

title: CeTPD Laboratory Information Management System
description: The Centre for Targeted Protein Degradation (CeTPD) is an academic research center focused on translational chemical biology, currently housing ~60 researchers and technicians across disciplines and experience levels (undergraduate, post graduate students, post-docs, (senior) staff scientists, Principal Investigators). The requirement is a software solution, for all research staff, that provides Laboratory Information Management System (LIMs) capability. This broadly includes scientist electronic lab notebook (across disciplines), reagent inventory and management, compound inventory and management and ideally some capability for processed data databasing and rudimentary visualisation. We are seeking to procure a secure, cloud-based design and Laboratory Information Management System to support collaborative drug discovery workflows. The solution is expected to deliver; - An integrated platform for electronic lab notebooks, reagent inventory management, compound registration and management and ideally data visualisation. - The system must accommodate the needs of scientists in both chemical and biological sciences and their respective workflows. - The system must accommodate that Users may require access relevant to both chemical biological sciences workflows within the same user area. - Seamless integration with existing computational workflows - Seamless integration with third-party applications and/or databases - A secure, stable and scalable cloud deployment which Complies with the University and collaborator cybersecurity, information governance and GDPR requirements Meets with strict performance, reliability and governance standards Meets with the functional and non-functional requirements of the CeTPD (as outlined below) - Improved operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and scalability to support future growth and evolving scientific needs

title: France – Sale of real estate – Appel à manifestation d’intérêt pour la vente du Site ferroviaire de Saint-Pierre-des Corps appartenant à la Société Nationale d’Actifs de Transition (ex-Fret SNCF) et situé à la ville-aux-Dames (37700)
description: La société Fret SNCF est une ancienne entreprise ferroviaire de transport de marchandises appartenant au Groupe SNCF, dont l’activité a pris fin le 31 décembre 2024. Devenue la Société Nationale d’Actifs de Transition (ci-après « la SNAT »), elle demeure, à ce jour, propriétaire d'un actif immobilier, dénommé Saint-Pierre-des-Corps, situé à la Ville-aux-Dames, identifié comme présentant un fort intérêt ferroviaire (ci-après le « Site ferroviaire »). Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre d’un plan de discontinuité économique, la SNAT entend céder ce Site ferroviaire à un acquéreur intéressé. Le présent appel à manifestation d’intérêt a pour objet de procéder à la sélection dudit acquéreur. La localisation, les références cadastrales et les caractéristiques du Site ferroviaire sont indiquées dans les documents de la consultation. L’acquéreur sera sélectionné à l’issue de deux phases successives : (i.) une phase de candidature, dite également Phase 1, ouverte à tout Candidat respectant les conditions de participation prévues et (ii.) une phase d’offre, dite également Phase 2, réservée aux candidats admis à remettre une offre à l’issue de la phase de candidature. Les informations détaillées relatives à la procédure figurent dans le règlement de la consultation, accessible dans les mêmes conditions que les autres documents de la consultation (cf. rubrique « Informations complémentaires »). Le présent appel à manifestation d’intérêt, qui ne tend à la passation ni d’un marché public ni d’un contrat de concession, ne relève pas des directives 2014/23/UE, 2014/24/UE et 2014/25/UE du 26 février 2014. En outre, aucune disposition législative ou réglementaire ne subordonne la vente du Site ferroviaire à une procédure de publicité et de mise en concurrence préalable. La présente procédure est donc menée à titre libre et volontaire suivant les seules modalités décrites dans le règlement de la consultation.

title: Thermal Conductivity Measurement System
description: The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) requires the supply of a state-of-the-art thermophysical analysis system for the direct and simultaneous measurement of thermal conductivity (?), thermal diffusivity (a), and specific heat capacity (cp) for rechargeable battery systems and their constituent materials. The layered architecture of modern batteries introduces strong anisotropic heat transfer, with significant differences between in-plane and through-plane conduction. Conventional steady-state measurement techniques are often too slow or imprecise to capture these directional effects within intact cells. The required system must therefore use a transient thermal measurement methodology, such as the Transient Plane Source (TPS) or equivalent, to enable non-destructive and direction-resolved characterization of pouch, prismatic, and cylindrical cells. The new instrumentation will expand NRC’s Automotive and Surface Transportation (AST) sector capabilities by enabling precise measurement of both isotropic and anisotropic thermophysical properties under controlled temperature environments, ranging from sub-ambient to elevated conditions representative of real battery operation. These capabilities are essential for developing next-generation testing standards and modeling frameworks that address safety, cooling optimization, and lifecycle management in electric vehicle and stationary energy storage applications.

title: Fachhochschulzentrum Graubünden (FHZGR), Chur / BKP 339.1 EMV-Raum
description: Beschaffung, Lieferung, Installation und Inbetriebnahme einer schirmgedämpften EMV-Testanlage für den Neubau des Fachhochschulzentrums Graubünden (FHGR) in Chur. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst eine schlüsselfertige Full-Compliance-3m-Absorberhalle (SAC) im 1. UG inklusive eines integrierten 2m-Drehtischs (Traglast min. 1000 kg) und eines automatischen Antennenmasts (1–4 m Scan) sowie eines direkt angebauten, geschirmten Mess- und Auswerteraums mit separater Verstärkernische. Beide Kabinen sind für Frequenzbereiche von 9 kHz bis 18 GHz (optional bis 40 GHz) auszulegen und verfügen über hochfrequenzdichte Schirmtüren sowie einen Doppelboden mit mindestens 2 mm verzinkter Massefläche. Im Angebotsumfang eingeschlossen sind die Ergänzung und schlüsselfertige Integration des vollständigen EMV-Messequipments (für Emissions- und Immunitätsprüfungen nach CISPR, IEC und ISO) unter Einbindung vorhandener Prüfgeräte sowie Spezialdienstleistungen wie die 3D-Einbauplatzmodellierung und die finale Abnahme/Leistungsprüfung (NSA, SVSWR, FU) durch ein unabhängiges, nach ISO 17025 akkreditiertes Labor.

title: DLA DWCF B1907 Backup Power Generator, Yokosuka, Japan
description: Introduction: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Japan District (POJ), is performing market research for an upcoming Design-Bid-Build (DBB) requirement entitled, �DLA DWCF B1907 Backup Power Generator, Yokosuka, Japan.". This announcement represents a market survey that is intended for planning purposes only. The purpose of this notice is to identify sources capable of performing this project and to receive responses from those firms to assist the Government's acquisition planning. This survey does not constitute a commitment by the Government for any follow-on announcements, solicitation, or award. This notice is NOT a solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information provided as a result of this market survey. This market survey is intended for local sources only. Local sources are those sources physically located and licensed to conduct business in Japan. Firms interested and capable of performing this work are highly encouraged to submit a response (submission requirements are located within this notice). We are committed to partnering with industry as much as we can throughout this process and therefore encourage all interested companies to respond to this sources sought. Market research and industry feedback is an essential part of the acquisition process. The information requested in this announcement will be used within POJ to facilitate decision-making and will not be disclosed outside the agency. However, respondents submitting business information pursuant to this announcement should consult 41 C.F.R. parts 105-60 and other implementing regulations concerning the release of such information to third parties under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). All information submitted by respondents that they consider confidential and not releasable to third parties outside of USACE, and its employees, agents, consultants, and representatives, must be clearly and conspicuously marked. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM) All interested companies, including joint ventures, shall be registered in the SAM database in order to be eligible for award of Government contracts. https://www.sam.gov LOCAL SOURCES Firms which have not done business with U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Japan Engineering District, are requested to visit the following website: https://www.poj.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/ for general information. This contract will be performed in its entirety in the country of Japan and is intended only for local sources. Only local sources will be considered under this solicitation. Local sources are sources (e.g. corporations, partnerships, or Joint Ventures [For a Joint Venture, the Joint Venture as an independent entity must satisfy the local source requirements or, in the alternative, each member of the Joint Venture must individually satisfy the local source requirements]) that are physically located in Japan and authorized (i.e. licensed and registered) to perform construction in Japan. Specifically, a prospective offeror must be duly authorized to operate and conduct construction business in Japan and must fully comply with all applicable laws, decrees, labor standards, and regulations of Japan during the performance of the resulting contracts. In addition, offerors must possess a Japanese civil construction (doboku isshiki koji) license or Japanese architectural construction (kenchiku isshiki koji) license by the proposal due date and time. The U.S. Government will verify that the offeror has the license through the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) website at https://etsuran2.mlit.go.jp/TAKKEN. It is the responsibility of the offeror to ensure that it has the license (Japanese civil construction or Japanese architectural construction), and that it is accurately shown on the MLIT website, by the proposal due date and time. Failure to comply with this requirement will be cause for rejection of your offer. The U.S. Government will not offer �United States Official Contractor� status under Article XIV of the US-Japan Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) to U.S. contractors normally resident in the United States; nor will the U.S. Government certify employees of such contractors as �Members of the Civilian Component� under Article I(b) of the SOFA. PROJECTS INFORMATION: Project Title: DLA DWCF B1907 Backup Power Generator Project Location: Yokosuka Japan Project FSC: Y1MZ - Construction of EPG (Electric Power Generation) Facilities�Other, Including Transmission Project NAICS: 237130 - Power and Communication Line and Related Structures Construction Project Magnitude: Between �500,000,000 and �2,000,000,000 (Japanese YEN) Project Description: Design-Bid-Build. Install a backup generator to support the mission at Building 1907. The new backup generator is expected to provide backup power to B1907 for the next 10 years at minimum. The generator has been sized to handle the following planned future loads: five new VLMs assumed to be rated the same as the existing VLMs(total of ~45 kW), operation of all four existing conveyor elevators (currently only two are operational at this time; two conveyors are fed from a 200A @ 210V, 3ph/3w feed), and an expected 20% increase in loads for the server rooms (total of ~20 kW). Anticipated Period of Performance: 518 Calendar Days Procurement Method: The Government intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) Solicitation. The Government anticipates that a solicitation will be issued approximately in May 2027. This survey does not constitute a commitment by the Government for any follow-on announcements, solicitation(s), or award(s). Any solicitation(s) pursued will be intended for local sources only. Local sources are those sources physically located and authorized to perform construction work in Japan. Draft plans and specifications are being provided for INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES. Offerors are cautioned that these drawings and specifications are in DRAFT FORMAT. ========================================================================== REQUESTED INFORMATION Interested firms are requested to reply with the following information no later than 11 December 2026 Japan Standard Time. Please submit your responses via e-mail to Mr. Ryan Marzetta, Contracting Officer at ryan.j.marzetta@usace.army.mil and Mr. Jiro Miyairi, Contract Specialist at jiro.miyairi@usace.army.mil Name of your company, address, phone number, email, SAM UEI, CAGE Code, and English Speaking Point of Contact (POC) name. Does your company have CMMC certification? If yes, what level and when does it expire. Identify your current construction bonding levels: a. Single Contract Amount b. Aggregate Maximum Contract Amoun c. Name of Sureties Identify which project(s) your firm is interested in and describe your firm's interest, capability and experience relative to the work described in the interested Project Description. Please provide at least one (1) project, but no more than three (3) projects, that is comparable to this project your company has completed (for government or commercial customers) in the past six (6) years. a. Project Title and Location b. Customer/Agency c. Project Value and Brief Description d. Date Completed or Percent Complete e. Your role (Prime, Subcontractor, Designer of Record, Joint Venture, etc) Technical Questions a. Does the Period of Performance seem reasonable? If not, provide what your company believes to be the Period of Performances (PoP) for the project. b. Are you expecting any long lead items? If so, which items and how long will it take to procure. c. Will a 1100 KVA package unit generator readily available in Japan. Will it need to be custom made? Do you have any other concerns related to the Draft technical specifications and drawings? Are there any other comments or suggestions that may increase your interest? title: Generator Inspection & Maintenance Services, various locations, Nunavut
description: Description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Iqaluit, Nunavut Territories, has a requirement for Generator Inspection & Maintenance Services at the RCMP Cambridge Bay, Clyde River, Gjoa Haven, Kinngait, Qikitarjuaq, Taloyoak Detachments, Iqaluit Headquarters Building and Iqaluit Hangar. This procurement is subject to the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement and the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases, in the Nunavut Settlement Area. Bidders are requested to maximize Inuit employment, subcontracting and on-the-job training opportunities, and involve Inuit businesses, in carrying out the work under this project. The Nunavut Agreement contains a provision requiring the inclusion of socio-economic bid criteria in the solicitation document, when practicable and consistent with sound procurement management principles. These socio-economic bid criteria are referred to as Nunavut Benefits Criteria (NBC) and Inuit Benefits Criteria (IBC), and bidders propose Inuit benefits in their bid submission via an Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP). This solicitation is limited for bidding among firms registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). Bids submitted by businesses not on the IFR will render the bid non-responsive and no further consideration will be accorded to the bid. Delivery Date: The contract period will be for 36-months from the date of contract, with the option to extend for 2 additional 1 year periods. Security: This requirement contains a security requirement. Basis of selection: A bid must comply with all the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory requirements. Bids not meeting the requirements will be declared non-responsive. The selection will be based on the highest responsive combined rating of total Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP) merit, and price. The ratio will be 30% for the total IBP merit, and 70% for price. Tenders must be submitted to the RCMP Bid Receiving Unit at: NWR_Procurement_Bids@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. The RCMP has adopted the Integrity Regime administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada. As a result, the integrity provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. Canada will make available Notices of Proposed Procurement (NPP), bid solicitations and related documents for download through the Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) at https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities . Canada is not responsible and will not assume any liabilities whatsoever for the information found on websites of third parties. In the event an NPP, bid solicitation or related documentation would be amended, Canada will not be sending notifications. Canada will post all amendments, including significant enquiries received and their replies, using GETS. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. Indigenous Procurement: The federal Indigenous Business Directory (IBD) is an online resource for all levels of government and the private sector to identify Indigenous business capacity. Having a business profile in the IBD will increase your company’s visibility and may provide additional business. A profile in the IBD can also allow you to compete for federal government contracts that are set-aside for Indigenous businesses through the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Businesses. For more information and to review eligibility criteria and register, visit: www.canada.ca/indigenousbusinessdirectory.

title: N0001927R1025 E-6B Mercury Depot Maintenance Repair and Overhaul (MRO): Request for Proposal (RFP)
description: ***Start of Notice Description 20261112*** The purpose of this notice is to advise interested parties that an updated solicitation file for Solicitation N0001927R1025 has been uploaded to the Solicitation Module of the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website under the title E_6B_MRO_Solicitation_Rev_1__N0001927R1025 to support proposal development. This update incorporates required Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) provisions and clauses pertinent to this acquisition. Incorporated / Updated FAR and DFARS Clauses: FAR 52.226-7 Drug-Free Workplace, dated May 2024 FAR 52.232-16 Progress Payments (Deviation 2026-O0038), dated Feb 2026 FAR 52.233-1 Disputes (Deviation 2026-O0038) (Alternate I), dated Feb 2026 FAR 52.240-92 Security Requirements (Deviation 2026-O0038), dated Feb 2026 FAR 52.203-11 Certification and Disclosure Regarding Payments to Influence Certain Federal Transactions, dated Sep 2024 FAR 52.203-18 Prohibition on Contracting with Entities that Require Certain Internal Confidentiality Agreements or Statements-Representation, dated Jan 2017 FAR 52.215-1 Instructions to Offerors-Competitive Acquisition (Deviation 2026-O0038) (Alternate I), dated Feb 2026 DFARS 252.226-7003 Drug-Free Work Force, dated Aug 2024 DFARS 252.247-7016 Contractor Liability for Loss or Damage, dated Dec 1991 DFARS 252.225-7000 Buy American-Balance of Payments Program Certificate, dated Feb 2024 DFARS 252.215-7012 Requirements for Submission of Proposals via Electronic Media, dated Jan 2018 (Note: All incorporated provisions and clauses are set forth in full text or incorporated by reference within the updated solicitation documentation available in PIEE.) ***End of Notice Description 20261112*** ***Start of Notice Description 20261109*** To ensure clarity for submission of questions related to the N0001927R1025 solicitation, the Government provides the following update to paragraph three (3) of the 27 October 2026 N0001927R1025 formal Request for Proposal (RFP) posting: Questions related to the solicitation are due not later than midnight (12:00am) 09 November 2026 and shall be submitted using the Excel file titled �Question and Answer Form_Final_RFP_Offeror Name� posted with the solicitation. Questions shall be submitted via email to Contract Specialist Mr. Timothy C. Ayers (timothy.c.ayers.civ@us.navy.mil) and Mr. David T. Guy (david.t.guy.civ@us.navy.mil) on or before the 09 November 2026 submission date. While submission of questions will be accepted up to midnight (12:00am) 09 November 2026, interested parties are encouraged to submit as early as possible to facilitate timely review and response by the Government. ***End of Notice Description 20261109*** ***Start of Notice Description 20261027*** The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of PMA-271 (Airborne Strategic Command, Control and Communications Program Office), posts formal Request for Proposal (RFP) N0001927R1025 for the E-6B Mercury Depot Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) effort. This notice is a follow-on to the E-6B MRO DRAFT Request for Proposal Notice N00019-25-RFPREQ-APM271-0012. NAVAIR intends to award a single source Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for MRO services for the E-6B aircraft under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 6 full and open competition. This IDIQ is anticipated to include one (1) five-year base ordering period with the option for one (1) additional five-year ordering period from Fiscal Years (FYs) 2027 through 2036. Planned award is during fourth quarter of Government FY 2027. Questions related to the solicitation are due not later than 09 November 2026 and shall be submitted using the Excel file titled �Question and Answer Form_Final_RFP_Offeror Name� posted with the solicitation. Questions shall be submitted via email to Contract Specialist Mr. Timothy C. Ayers (timothy.c.ayers.civ@us.navy.mil) and Mr. David T. Guy (david.t.guy.civ@us.navy.mil) on or before the 09 November 2026 submission date. Proposals are due not later than the date and time as specified in Block 9 of the SF 33. However, potential Offerors are encouraged to submit portions of their proposal associated with past performance 14 calendar days prior to that submission date. See Section L paragraph 3.1 of the solicitation document for details. Access to Final RFP: The solicitation, including all attachments, is posted in the Solicitation Module of the U.S. Government PIEE website with restricted access and will only be made available to companies incorporated in the United States as verified via SAM.gov. The final RFP and associated attachments may contain Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and may contain information whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act (Title 22, U.S.C. Sec 2751, et seq.) or the Export Administration Act of 1979, as amended (Title 50, U.S.C. App. 2401 et seq.). Request Access Procedures: Accordingly, all requests for access to the final RFP and associated attachments must be in writing and shall include a statement that the company intends to submit as a prime contractor, as well as a certified copy of a DD Form 2345, Military Critical Technical Data Agreement. To obtain certification, contact Defense Logistics Information Service at (800) 352-3572 or https://www.dla.mil/Logistics-Operations/Services/JCP/#jointcertification-program-jcp-office; company name, address, and CAGE code (as it appears in SAM.gov and as registered in the PIEE Solicitation Module). After obtaining a certified DD Form 2345, each potential Offeror shall transmit via email its written request for access to the final RFP and associated attachments, with the certified DD Form 2345 attached to the email to Contract Specialist Mr. Timothy C. Ayers (timothy.c.ayers.civ@us.navy.mil) and Mr. David T. Guy (david.t.guy.civ@us.navy.mil). Prior to granting access to the final RFP and associated attachments, the Government will verify that the company requesting the data is incorporated within the United States based on CAGE code listing in SAM.gov. Upon review of the potential Offeror�s written request and verification of potential Offeror�s status in SAM.gov, the Government will provide the potential Offeror access to the final RFP and associated attachments in the Solicitation Module of the U.S. Government PIEE website. Companies that had previously requested and been granted access to the DRAFT Request for Proposal under Notice N00019-25-RFPREQ-APM271-0012, have already been provided access in PIEE to the formal RFP under Notice N0001927R1025. The Government may also provide separately, via the dissemination method described below, technical documents to assist potential Offerors with developing their proposals. Access to Other Technical Documents: (Potential Prime Contractor Requests Only) Technical documents have been made available to assist with developing proposals. Sec 2751, et seq.) or the Export Administration Act of 1979, as amended (Title 50, U.S.C. App. 2401 et seq.). Accordingly, all requests for access to technical documents must follow the �Request Access Procedures� described above. Upon review of the potential Offeror�s written request and approved DD Form 2345, the Government will provide the potential Offeror access to the technical documents via the DoD SAFE website (previously AMRDEC) - https://safe.apps.mil/. The data custodian listed in Block 3 of DD Form 2345 will receive a link, via e-mail, to the package download page as well as a password. title: End of the World Long Term Stewardship
description: Amendment 002: This amendment provides responses to questions received, corrections to several solicitation documents, and provides new contacts for the receipt of proposals. The response sue date and time are not extended. The following documents are amended and previous versions deleted: C05a_1a EOTW G-Z LTIRSC_12363N26R4016_A002 C05b_1b EOTW G-Z LTIRSC SOI_12363N26R4016_A002 C05c_2 EOTW G-Z LTIRSC Appendix A_A002 C05d_3 EOTW G-Z LTIRSC Appendix B_A002 C05e_4 EOTW G-Z LTIRSC Appendix C_A002 Proposals are to be submitted via email to Bonnie Yoakum at bonnie.yoakum@usda.gov and Kasandra Meyer at kasandra.meyer@usda.gov. Amendment 001: This amendment provides responses to questions received, updates the points of contact for proposal submission, extends the solicitation response due date and time to 9:00 AM MST on 12/11/2026 and sets a deadline of 11/13/2026 for additional questions. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4016 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the End of the World G-Z Long-Term IRSC (EOTW G-Z LTIRSC). The End of the World Project area is approximately 50,000 acres on the Salmon River Ranger District of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest. The End of the World EIS authorizes commercial treatment on over 17,000 acres primarily through intermediate harvest. The purpose of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to thin overstocked stands to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire as well as improve stand health. The EOTW Project is within the Wildland Urban Interface and has numerous private inholdings with seasonal and permanent residents. This contracting tool will increase the pace and scale of active management beyond the current capacity of staffing levels. A secondary objective of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to provide a steady, dependable supply of timber and forest products to local facilities. This project aligns with Secretarial Memo 1078-006 and the Implementation of Secretarial Memo 1078-006 dated April 3, 2025 to utilize long term stewardship contracts for active management. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. description: Amendment 001: This amendment provides responses to questions received, updates the points of contact for proposal submission, extends the solicitation response due date and time to 9:00 AM MST on 12/11/2026 and sets a deadline of 11/13/2026 for additional questions. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4016 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the End of the World G-Z Long-Term IRSC (EOTW G-Z LTIRSC). The End of the World Project area is approximately 50,000 acres on the Salmon River Ranger District of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest. The End of the World EIS authorizes commercial treatment on over 17,000 acres primarily through intermediate harvest. The purpose of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to thin overstocked stands to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire as well as improve stand health. The EOTW Project is within the Wildland Urban Interface and has numerous private inholdings with seasonal and permanent residents. This contracting tool will increase the pace and scale of active management beyond the current capacity of staffing levels. A secondary objective of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to provide a steady, dependable supply of timber and forest products to local facilities. This project aligns with Secretarial Memo 1078-006 and the Implementation of Secretarial Memo 1078-006 dated April 3, 2025 to utilize long term stewardship contracts for active management. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 113310 and the small business size standard is 500 Employees This acquisition is an unrestricted requirement. Description of Requirement: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Network Contracting Office 19 (NCO 19) is conducting a market survey to identify vendors capable of providing Cost Per Test (CPT) reference lab testing covering testing of all venous and arterial blood samples and urine samples from veteran s patients as ordered by VA clinician. description: The Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify interested and capable organizations and obtain industry feedback regarding operational and technical support for the administration of the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement (TEFCA). The contemplated services encompass three functional areas: Governing Documents and Caucus Facilitation: Develop, revise, and maintain the Common Agreement, standard operating procedures, and technical documents; facilitate stakeholder caucuses and workgroups; and administer public feedback and change management processes. Onboarding, Operations, and Implementation: Support Qualified Health Information Network (QHIN) application review, onboarding, designation, compliance monitoring, and network operations; manage cybersecurity and incident response; and develop, operate, maintain, and update supporting infrastructure and interoperability testing capabilities. Investigations and Dispute Resolution: Investigate potential noncompliance, interpret TEFCA requirements, recommend remediation, and support dispute resolution processes. Organizations may respond regarding one or more functional areas or combinations of functions. ONC welcomes recommendations concerning an integrated or separate acquisition approach, alternative contract vehicles and classifications, commercial capabilities, staffing, contract types, performance risks, and opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce costs. Respondents should provide capability information and annual rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost estimates, including assumptions and principal cost drivers, in accordance with the attached RFI and Planning Assumptions. The preliminary classifications are NAICS 541519, PSC DD01, and GSA Multiple Award Schedule SINs 54151HEAL and 541611. Possession of both identified SINs is not required to respond. Responses are due December 11, 2026, at 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time, by email to Donna.Sykes@hhs.gov. Use the subject line �RFI - Operational and Technical Support for TEFCA.� Clearly mark proprietary information. The Government will not provide individual acknowledgments of receipt or respond to follow-up inquiries requesting confirmation of receipt, the status of this RFI, or future acquisition plans. Please do not submit inquiries of this nature. If the Government proceeds with a solicitation, it will be issued through the applicable GSA platform or SAM.gov, as appropriate. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring those platforms for future notices and opportunities. Review all three attachments for the complete requirements and response instructions: the RFI, Draft Statement of Work, and Planning Assumptions. This RFI is solely for information and planning purposes and is not a solicitation. Responses are voluntary, are information only, and are not offers that can be accepted to form a binding contract. The Government will not award a contract based on this RFI or pay for responses. Responding is not a prerequisite to participating in any future solicitation.

title: Flight Services for Wildlife Services, Colorado
description: The Contractor shall furnish, operate, and maintain one fixed-wing aircraft and one pilot in accordance with the specifications here in for use by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Wildlife Services (WS), in support of predator damage management activities in Montrose, Delta, Ouray, Mesa, Pitkin, Gunnison, and San Miguel counties in Colorado. Flights will be required to reduce coyote predation on livestock, for disease monitoring, or to remove invasive species. Flights may not be required for extended periods because of lack of predation or inclement weather conditions, but the aircraft must be available to provide services when needed upon 48 hours notice. Most aerial operations will occur January through April and sporadically in October, November, and December. title: Thomaston Lake Dam, Gate House Roof Repairs, Thomaston, CT
description: Action Code: Sources Sought Notice Subject: Thomaston Lake Dam, Gate House Roof Repairs, Thomaston, CT Sources Sought Number: W912WJ-27-X-1CY2 NACIS Code: 238160 Response date: December 11, 2026 Place of Performance: US Army Corps of Engineers, New England District 696 Virginia Road Concord, MA 01742-2751 US The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing this Sources Sought Announcement for Construction Services for the repairs to the Gate House Roof at Thomaston Lake Dam in Thomaston, Connecticut. This announcement is to determine interest, availability and capability of 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned and Small Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 238160 with a size standard of $19M. The project is planned to be issued in the Spring of 2027 with construction to take place in the Summer of 2027. The estimated construction cost is between $350,000 - $500,000. Thomaston Lake Dam is situated on the Naugatuck River and is a part of a network of flood control dams and local protection projects built by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in the Upper Connecticut River Basin. The construction was completed in 1960. The dam is located between Hill Road (to the east) and James H Darcey Memorial Highway (to the west). The dam consists of a rockfill earth gravity dam with stone slope protection 2,000-feet long and 137-feet high and a 435-foot-wide uncontrolled spillway. The work of this project involves removing the existing EPDM roof, thermal insulation and all associated components and replace with new thermal insulation and roof membrane system. The existing roof has a parapet wall around the perimeter which an existing scupper exists. The existing scupper will be required to be enlarged. The work also includes installing a new roof hatch and fall protection railing system. The existing lightning protection system will be removed and replaced with a new lightning protection system. The roof is approximately 35 feet above the service bridge deck which only accesses one side of the gate house tower. Work pertaining to the scupper will require special fall protection requirements as this side of the gate house tower is over water at a height greater than 45 feet. The contractor will need to comply and submit all required USACE safety submittals for this project. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, small business, etc.), as well as qualifications and experience in performing the work components stated above. Please include at least two specific examples of the firm�s experience performing the work requirements stated above. The projects must have been performed within the last seven years. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications, which will be used to support the offeror�s effort and their experience must also have been performed within the last seven years. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages. Responses are due by December 11, 2026. Responses should be emailed to: CONTRACT SPECIALIST Brian Mannion Email: Brian.T.Mannion@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8478 The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. description: Sources Sought Response Form Renovate Mission Support Facility (B145) & Repair/Renovate Conference Room (LRSO), Alert Facility (B1085) Minot Air Force Base (MAFB), North Dakota Sources Sought Notice # W9128F27SM005 NOTICE TYPE: Market Research / Sources Sought ACQUISITION AUTHORITY: 10 USC 2808a (Other Transaction Authority for Military Construction Projects) PROJECT TITLES: FY27 Renovate Mission Support B145, MAFB, ND FY27 RENOVATE CONFERENCE ROOM (LRSO) BUILDING 1085, MINOT AFB, ND NAICS CODE: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction ESTIMATED VALUE: Firm Construction Cost Limitation (CCL): Renovate Mission Support Building 145 (CCL): $ 31,923,000 Renovate Conference Room (LRSO) Building 1085 (CCL): $ 3,503,000 PURPOSE By way of this Industry Outreach Questionnaire, the USACE-Omaha District intends to gauge Industry�s interest and capabilities in providing the requirement described hereunder. The Government welcomes qualifications and capability statements from all qualified entities regardless of federal construction experience or business size. The responses to this notice will be used for planning purposes for the upcoming procurement(s). This notice does not constitute a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotes, or Invitation for Bids (IFB). It does not guarantee the future issuance of an opportunity notice, nor does it commit the government to execute an agreement or pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in responding to this notice. This Agency will not accept unsolicited submissions in response to this notice. All costs associated with responding will be solely at the responding party's expense. Responding parties are requested to refrain from submitting proprietary information. Responses are to be sent via email to (POC) Phillip Wickham at Phillip.L. Wickham@usace.army.mil and (POC) Jessica Beckman at Jessica.L. Beckman@usace.army.mil not later than 11 December 2026 by 2:00 pm (MST)). Narratives shall be no longer than 5 pages. Email responses are required. PROBLEM AND BACKGROUND STATEMENT: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is conducting market research on behalf Minot Air Force Base which has a requirement to address two distinct, but critical facility needs. The first is a full-scale renovation of the Mission Support Facility (Building 145), which requires significant interior, exterior, and systems modernization to continue supporting its operational function. The Mission Support Facility has a project timeline for award of the phase 1 agreement of FY26 Q3. The second is the need to convert an existing conference room (Building 1085) into a high-security Special Access Facility (SAF) accredited to Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 705 standards. To streamline execution and foster innovation, the Government intends to address this suite of projects programmatically under a single Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). This approach seeks a capable partner or consortium to deliver a comprehensive design-build solution for both projects, potentially on a concurrent or closely phased schedule. The Special Access Facility (SAF) has a project timeline for award of the phase 1 agreement of FY26 Q3 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Omaha District, is conducting market research on behalf of the Department of the Air Force (5th Bomb Wing / Air Force Global Strike Command) at Minot Air Force Base (AFB), North Dakota. The existing Minot AFB Alert Facility (Building 1085) requires critical renovation and spatial reconfiguration of its existing briefing, projector, and office spaces (Offices 225, 226, 227, Projector/Briefing Room 228, and a new Entry Control Vestibule, totaling approximately 2,660 SF) to establish a state-of-the-art Special Access Facility (SAF) supporting the Long-Range Stand-Off (LRSO) mission. CurrRntly, the existing spaces fail to meet the operational, acoustic, and physical security requirements of the mission users. Furthermore, the space requires extensive modernization to achieve full compliance with Intelligence Community Directive / Intelligence Community Standard (ICD/ICS 705) for Classified Open Discussion (OD) up to the Top Secret (TS) level. To resolve these operational shortfalls within an accelerated timeline, USACE intends to execute this project utilizing an innovative Construction Manager at Risk (CM@Risk) acquisition approach authorized under Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government's in-house USACE Design Team serves as the 100% Designer of Record (DOR) for both projects. The Government will advance the design for project 1 and 2 to an approximate 95% completion level, which will serve as the technical Requirements Package. The objective of this acquisition strategy is to select the single "best-suited" construction partner based on qualifications. The selected partner will collaborate with the USACE in-house DOR during Phase 1 to validate constructability, refine trade pricing, mitigate specialized supply-chain risks, and establish an open-book Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) prior to transitioning into Phase 2 physical construction execution. PROJECT DESCRIPTION AND OBJECTIVES: Project 1: Renovate Mission Support Center, Building 145 This project involves complete renovation and conversion of roughly 28,000 SF of the 45,236 SF facility into a centralized point for mission support functions for all airman, families, and retirees. General Demolition & Hazardous Abatement: Wall to wall, as required to implement the new layout and update dated systems. This includes but is not limited to the following: masonry and/or steel-studs walls; flooring, interior doors, and abandoned equipment; water, sewer and venting lines; electrical conductors and panels; HVAC distribution and equipment systems; and exterior doors & windows. All abandoned construction debris and equipment be to be recycled and/or disposed of off-site. Removal and disposal asbestos and other hazardous materials. Entry Control Vestibules: as required, replace entry/exit flow and ADA compliance, to accommodate fire alarm panels, and to account for any loading/unloading requirements. Mechanical: Update water lines and PIV to ensure they can independently support the fire suppression system, building conversion, and increased occupant load. title: Fort Meade Hazardous Waste Disposal Contract
description: Fort Meade HW Disposal Contract. THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY QUALIFIED SMALL BUSINESSES, specifically 8(a), HUBZone, woman-owned, and service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, for the requirement described below. The intent of this Sources Sought is to identify capable small business that can perform with limitations on subcontracting. The scope of work requires the transportation and disposal of RCRA Hazardous wastes, non-RCRA wastes, Batteries, Corrosive waste, Compressed Gas Cylinders, Flammable waste, Demil-required waste, State-Regulated waste, Non-Hazardous Waste, Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs), AFFF and other PFAS-related waste, Mandatory Recycling waste, Reactive waste, and Toxic waste located on or around military installations or within a 50-mile radius of any pickup/service location listed on the Pickup and Service Locations Table (See Attachment 3) of the contract in the states of Maryland, Virgina, Delaware, and the District of Columbia. Infectious Medical Waste, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Controlled Substances, Radioactive Waste, Ammunition and explosives, will not be included under this contract. Special services will be required such as sampling and analysis, industrial cleaning services, lab packs/loose packs, rolloff box rentals, vacuum box rentals, FRAC Tank rentals, and expedited removals and performance. This scope also encompasses the provision of various supplies upon government request. All services necessary for the collection, storage, processing, removal, transportation, final treatment and disposal of waste shall be in accordance with all local, state, Department of Defense, and Federal laws and regulations. FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (FEB 2023) CLASS DEVIATION 2021-O0008 states the Offeror/Contractor agrees to not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Contractors may be subject to a minimum $500,000 fine if awarded a contract with this clause and don�t meet the requirement. We have identified the majority of RCRA TSDFs (Treatment, Storage, Disposal Facilities) in the industry as large businesses. All TSDFs used during the performance of this contract must be approved and listed on the Qualified Facilities List located at the following website: https://www.dla.mil/Disposition-Services/Offers/Hazardous-Waste-Disposal/Qualified-Facilities-List/ Given there is a lack of small business ownership of TSDFs and that disposal costs make up a large portion of the contract dollar value, there is a reasonable probability that a small business would pay more than 50% of the cost of the contract to large businesses. *The Government intends to solicit proposals on SAM.gov and award a Firm-Fixed Priced, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity Services Contract. The contract is anticipated to have one 30-month base period, followed by one 30-month option period. There is no solicitation available at this time. However, attached is a DRAFT Price Schedule, DRAFT PWS, and Anticipated Pickup Points that firms responding to this Sources Sought should use to help determine if they would be able to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting requirements. IF YOUR FIRM IS CAPABLE OF PERFORMING THE REQUESTED SERVICES, WITHOUT THE LIMITATIONS ON SUBCONTRACTING, THE CAPABILITIES PACKAGE DETAILED BELOW IS NOT REQUIRED. In accordance with FAR 6.101(a), with certain limited exceptions, contracting officers shall promote and provide for full and open competition in soliciting offers and awarding Government contracts. If your firm would like to respond to this Sources Sought, but is unable to meet the limitations on subcontracting, please email Raymond.empie@dla.mil with �Fort Meade - SOURCES SOUGHT HAZ� in the subject line, stating your firms� Notification of Interest (a capabilities package is not required). SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested firms must demonstrate their ability to perform the requested services, described above, by submitting a brief capabilities package (no more than three pages in length, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum). This documentation shall identify, at a minimum: (1) Company name, office location(s), CAGE Code, and a statement identifying small business category and current status of the small business classification; (2) Relevant experience within the last five years, including any contract number(s), names of individuals responsible for the referenced contracts/projects, and current telephone numbers for those individuals; if you were a subcontractor, identify the work you actually performed as the sub-contractor; and (3) A statement identifying your firm�s ability to perform in accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (CLASS DEVIATION 2021-O0008), as well as an explanation of how you would be able to comply with this requirement if you are a small business of any type considering the disposal requirements within the draft price schedule that is anticipated to be included in the contract; (note: large business respondents do not need to address this). (4) A listing of TSDFs your firm would use during the performance of this contract, identifying each TSDF as similarly situated or not as your firm. The submittal package must be emailed to Raymond.empie@dla.mil. with �Fort Meade - SOURCES SOUGHT HAZ WASTE� in the subject line. The submittal package must be received no later than 1400 EST, Friday-December 11, 2026 LATE RESPONSES WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. Upon review of industry response to this Sources Sought, the Government will determine whether a set-aside acquisition is in the Government's best interest. If an unrestricted solicitation is issued, then the Class Deviation 2021-O0008 Limitations on Subcontracting would not apply. All responsible firms, including small businesses, are eligible to submit a proposal in response to an unrestricted solicitation. A response to this Sources Sought will not be considered an adequate response to any forthcoming solicitation announcement. The Government WILL NOT provide a debriefing on the results of the survey. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought notice or any follow-up information requests. All information submitted will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purpose intended.

It does not guarantee the future issuance of an opportunity notice, nor does it commit the government to execute an agreement or pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in responding to this notice. The U.S. Government will not provide reimbursement for any information that may be submitted in response to this RFI. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. Respondents will not be notified of any results derived from a review of the information provided; however, information gathered may be utilized for technical and acquisition purposes. Information regarding SAM registration is available at https://www.sam.gov/portal/public/SAM SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: FEMA Region 10 seeks information from firms with capabilities, experience, and resources necessary to meet or exceed the stated requirements to perform design services related to a proposed 3-inch raised flooring system. Capability Statement Submission Requirements Interested businesses are requested to submit a Capability Statement demonstrating their ability to fulfill the Government�s needs. Submissions must include the following information: Company Information Company Name, Address, and Website. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, and Email). Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code. Business Size and Socio-Economic Status under NAICS 337215 (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business [SDVOSB], Women-Owned Small Business [WOSB], 8(a), HUBZone). Specify if your firm holds any Federal contract vehicles (e.g., GSA MAS, 8(a) STARS III, or regional IDIQs) that cover these types of commercial flooring installations. Capabilities and Experience List any relevant qualifications or credentials Description of experience providing design services related to a proposed 3-inch raised flooring system of similar size and scope List of relevant contracts (government or commercial), including contract value and period of performance Key personnel qualifications Technical Approach Overview of proposed approach to raised flooring (preventive, corrective, emergency maintenance) Use of technology (e.g., CMMS, energy management, automation). Quality assurance and performance metrics Innovative Technologies: Describe any innovative materials, methods, or technologies your firm could propose for a project of this scale that could lead to cost savings, schedule acceleration, or enhanced facility performance and resilience. Barriers to Innovation: What commercial or Government-imposed barriers currently make it difficult to propose or implement innovative construction technologies? How could the flexibility of an OTA help overcome these barriers? description: *****AMENDMENT 0001 Dated 11/18/2026***** The purpose of this amendment is to:(1) extend the proposal submission date to Friday 11 December 2026, (2) Update Section C NAVSEA Clause 215-H002 CONTRACTOR PROPOSAL (NAVSEA) (OCT 2018) (a) NAVSEA Solicitation No: to remove N6133126R3111 and insert N6133127R0006, (3) Update Section F - F.1 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE to remove Dahlgren and insert Panama City, (4) Upload Attachment J.12 Wage Determinations, (5) Update Section J Attachment J.1 Performance Work Statement (PWS) Section 3.0(e) by removing the sentence NSWC PCD will not provide space onboard NSWC PCD or the Naval Support Activity Panama City (NSAPC) during performance of this task order and replace it with PWS Section 3.0 (e) The Government will provide space for up to 15 Contractor personnel in office or working spaces each with a phone and Navy and Marine Corps Intranet (NMCI) computer with network connection., and (6)Update Section L - 2.5 from Company_Volume_III _Past Performance Reference for N61331-26-R-3111 to Company_Volume_III _Past Performance Reference for N61331-27-R-0006. ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ **Original Post*** **ONLY SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ARE ELIGIBLE FOR AWARD UNDER THIS SOLICITATION.*** Request for Proposal (RFP) (N6133127R0006) under the Seaport NxG Multiple Award Contract (MAC), for Mission Module Engineering and Technical Support. This effort has been previously been posted under the Opportunities page as the following: Sources Sought Notice (N6133126SNQ27), dated (Posted 7 May 2026) and the follow-up Advance Planning Notice/Pre-Solicitation Notice dated (16 June 2026). ***RESPONSES MUST BE SUBMITTED VIA THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE.*** ***ALL DOCUMENTS ARE AVAILABLE WITHIN THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE*** Questions and Answers WILL TAKE PLACE THROUGH PIEE MODULE AND POSTED TO PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE BY ATTACHMENT***This is a solicitation for SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ONLY. This solicitation is to provide services to support the Naval Surface Warfare Center Panama City Division (NSWC PCD) Modular Integration Division as the lead for engineering, analysis, and planning support for the modularization of off-board systems in support of the littoral warfare mission area. The requirements will include systems engineering, packaging and handling of off-board system hardware, system integration of legacy and emerging littoral mission systems, sea frame integration of mission modules, development of mission system common computing environments (e.g. Mission Package Computing Environment (MPCE)) and integrated communications networks (e.g. Multiple Vehicle Communication System(MVCS)), distributed engineering testing, and supporting the Government in validation and verification. Specifically, these requirements include the general program, engineering, technical, and integrated logistics support requirements for the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS)Mission Modules (MM) program at NSWC PCD.

description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command - New Jersey, on behalf of the office of the Project Manager, Combat Ammunition Systems (PM CAS), intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Primer Feed Mechanisms (PFMs) in support of the M777A2 155mm Howitzer. title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

title: DA10--Utilization Management Software (VA-27-00009483)
description: Page 7 of 7 REQUEST FOR INFORMATION THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Health Administration (VHA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) as market research to determine the availability of vendors that can provide a Utilization Management Software Tool with VHA enterprise-wide licensing that includes unlimited use, updates, and clinical and technical support for evidence-based criteria and the associated tools identified in the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) that interface seamlessly into the National Utilization Management Integration (NUMI) application and the Electronic Health Record (EHR). In addition, the Contractor shall provide training to certify and maintain certification for trainers throughout the VHA.. This RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. The VA is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore, will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with submission of the information being requested or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to this RFI. The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy Product Description (PD) or Performance Work Statement (PWS). Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it commit the Government to any specific course of action. Product information, brochures, part numbers, and/or other description information may be included with the submission. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. BACKGROUND VHA is committed to a healthcare system that treats its patient population effectively, efficiently, and appropriately. The VHA s Utilization Management (UM) Program focuses on using resources efficiently and ensuring that every Veteran receives consistent reliable, high-quality care in the optimal setting and at appropriate care delivery intervals. The objective of the UM program is to provide the correct care, for the right patient, at the best time and for the proper reasons using evidence-based practice and continuous measurement and improvement. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION In response to this RFI, VA seeks to gain industry feedback on the DRAFT Performance Work Statement (PWS). Please respond with suggested approaches/recommendations to the attached PWS, Vendor Questions, and RFI Respondent Information. Responses should not exceed 10 pages, single-spaced standard 1-inch margins and in a 12-point font. Responses to this RFI shall be submitted via email, with filename - Utilization.Management.rfi-name of your company - to William.Freer@va.gov and debra.clayton2@va.gov no later than December 11, 2026 at 3 PM EDT. VENDOR QUESTIONS Describe your solution s ability to meet all the requirements set forth in the attached Draft PWS. � Please specifically address the following requirements: Ability to Interface with NUMI (do you have this capability out of the box or is time required to develop?) Interface with the Cerner Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) (do you have this capability out of the box or is time required to develop?) Unlimited licenses available of the review products and ease of access for all users Multiple avenues to access the review products- book view, interactive anonymous, application, NUMI, Cerner, Mobile access Training of new VHA instructors each year with vendor verification through certification and relevant continuing education credits, and yearly sustainment training of current instructors with certification and continuing education credits. The opportunity to increase yearly sustainment training if needed. Reporting capability (please include any enhanced reports available) Describe how your system is hosted and how VA users would access the system. � If your solution is cloud-based, please describe your FedRamp certification status. Describe what type of training is provided with your solution and any recommendations related to how a workforce consisting of over a thousand users would be transitioned to your solution. � 2. How would user access be managed for your services and is it possible that specific VA users would be provided a direct ability to grant or remove user access? � � 3. Describe your technical support capabilities and what kind of help desk/customer services your solution provides. � 4. Does your solution utilize any form of Artificial Intelligence, Process Automation or other functions to enhance functionality? � 5. Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) estimate to include pricing models that would be most advantageous to the Government. � � 5. Describe your pricing methodology. Is there a price per user unit price? Do you offer an enterprise license? Do you offer tiered pricing methodology? � Do you offer the ability to choose different products, vice all included ? � RFI RESPONDENT INFORMATION Vendors shall provide the following information: Name of Company Address Point of Contact Phone Number Email address CAGE Unique Entity Identifier Number Company Business Size and Status for NAICS NAICS code(s) applicable to the products and services you can provide Any contract vehicle of which you are part that can be used to acquire your products/services. Typical contract vehicles include General Services Administration contracts, National Aeronautics and Space Administration Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement VI, or other Government-Wide Acquisition Contracts. Please also include Contract Number, expiration date, and point of contact. Socioeconomic data: If a small business, what type of small business are you? Are you able to comply with federal acquisition regulations clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting in execution of this effort? Are you able to comply with 852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction and with subcontracting limitations in accordance with 13 CFR 125.6 in execution of this effort?
