title: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE TO IDENTIFY POTENTIALLY CAPABLE, INTERESTED PARTIES FOR BIOSPECIMEN COLLECTION AND BIOBANKING SERVICES
description: TYPE OF NOTICE: This is a Sources Sought Notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) Office of Acquisitions and Logistics Management, on behalf of the National Cancer Institute�s (NCI�s) Division of Cancer Treatment and Diagnosis (DCTD), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice to conduct market research and identify interested and capable parties, including both large and small businesses, that have the resources and expertise to support biospecimen collection, biobanking, and related services. The required services will support cancer research across the United States by providing specialized expertise to identify, establish, and manage clinical sites across the nation to engage and enroll cancer patients onto NCI biospecimen collection protocols, collect biospecimens and associated medical data, and to provide biorepository services. Research studies may include, but are not limited to, development of patient-derived animal models, tumor characterization, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies, assay development and validation, clinical testing, and collection and management of biospecimens for future use. The Government intends to procure these specialized services through a competitive acquisition. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (MARKET RESEARCH), all Small Business Set-Aside categories will be considered for this procurement. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Performance of services for this effort will primarily take place at Contractor and/or Subcontractor facilities. DISCLAIMER:THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A �REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)�. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS NOTICE IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ), INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. THE GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO USE INFORMATION PROVIDED BY RESPONDENTS FOR ANY PURPOSE DEEMED NECESSARY AND LEGALLY APPROPRIATE. ANY ORGANIZATION RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE SHOULD ENSURE THAT ITS RESPONSE IS COMPLETE AND SUFFICIENTLY DETAILED TO ALLOW THE GOVERNMENT TO DETERMINE THE ORGANIZATION'S QUALIFICATIONS TO PERFORM THE WORK. PROGRAM BACKGROUND: NCI uses research biospecimens including tissues, blood, and other bodily fluids donated by patients as part of scientific research to develop novel diagnostics and therapies for cancer. The Contractor shall be responsible for providing services to identify and engage clinical sites in conducting NCI biospecimen collection studies and to provide biorepository services for concurrent multi-disciplinary studies and diverse study designs. Biospecimens and associated data of known quality are a critical resource for research that investigates the causes, biology, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of cancer. NCI requires biospecimens for research purposes that may include, but are not limited to, the following: development of patient-derived models, characterization of tumors using clinical- and research-grade sequencing, proteomics studies, pharmacodynamic studies, development and validation of clinical assays, performance of clinical testing and return of clinical test results to providers and patients, and development of research reserves of biospecimens for future research use. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: The objective of any potential contract is to obtain specialized services for the identification and coordination of clinical sites in the management of specific NCI biospecimen collection studies and the collection, processing, storage, and distribution of biospecimens and associated data for current and future cancer research. For specific details under each domain, please reference the draft Statement of Work which accompanies announcement. The Government encourages feedback from respondents in their capability submissions (i.e., comments, suggestions, recommendations) on the draft Statement of Work that would improve the understanding of the requirements for this anticipated acquisition. NCI is seeking the following information from respondents regarding strategies as well as explicit examples of how they would propose to support NCI initiatives in one or more of the following services areas: DOMAIN 1: CLINICAL SITE IDENTIFICATION AND ONBOARDING, CLINICAL SITE MANAGEMENT, TRAINING, PROVISION OF KITS, AND IDENTIFICATION OF EXISTING BIOSPECIMEN COLLECTIONS Domain 1 describes the biospecimen collection activities needed to identify and manage medical institutions (herein referred to as Clinical Sites) across the United States and Canada to engage and enroll cancer patients onto specific NCI biospecimen collection studies and to provide biospecimen collection kit services for the studies. NCI biospecimen collection studies will include collection of biospecimens and associated medical data. Some studies will require the identification of existing cancer biospecimen collections that meet quality and quantity metrics prescribed by the NCI and that are appropriately consented for use by NCI. The Contractor shall ensure these activities are conducted safely, efficiently, and in compliance with regulatory requirements as specified in IRB-approved NCI studies. DOMAIN 2: COMPREHENSIVE BIOREPOSITORY SERVICES, ACCREDITATION BY THE COLLEGE OF AMERICAN PATHOLOGISTS� BIOREPOSITORY ACCREDITATION PROGRAM (CAP/BAP), PATHOLOGY AND HISTOLOGY, TRAINING, QUALITY ASSURANCE, AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY. Domain 2 describes comprehensive biorepository services performed under biorepository accreditation by the College of American Pathologists� Biorepository Accreditation Program (CAP/BAP) and employing an onsite board-certified anatomic pathologist. Ability to provide expertise in tracking of pre-analytical variables and detailed inventory management for all biorepository activities per CAP/BAP requirements using an existing data management solution. Information technology support dedicated to biobanking operations, to include data and information collection, management, quality control and analysis. Ability to provide scientific expertise and leadership in biobanking activities including but not limited to appropriate processing of biospecimens into molecular analytes and appropriate biospecimen and analyte storage. Ability to provide administrative, program, and project support by performing administrative duties to provide continuity for office operations and procedures. DOMAIN 3: COMPREHENSIVE BIOREPOSITORY SERVICES, ACCREDITATION BY THE COLLEGE OF AMERICAN PATHOLOGISTS� BIOREPOSITORY ACCREDITATION PROGRAM (CAP/BAP), CLINICAL LABORATORY IMPROVEMENT AMENDMENTS OF 1988 (CLIA) AND PATHOLOGY SUPPORT Domain 3 describes comprehensive biorepository services with ability to provide services as described in Domain 2. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned

title: Finland – Bin-cleaning services – Jäteastioiden ja -säiliöiden pesupalvelut 2027
description: Pirkanmaan Jätehuolto Oy pyytää tarjouksia toimialueensa kiinteistöillä sijaitsevien jäteastioiden 140-770 l sekä säiliöiden 0,3-5 m3 pesupalvelusta. Pirkanmaan Jätehuolto järjestää alueensa kiinteistöille vuosittain pesukampanjoita, jolloin kiinteistön keräysvälineet pestään kertapesuna. Kampanjoita on vuodessa jäteastioille kaksi (kevät ja syksy) ja säiliöille kolme (kevät, kesä ja syksy). Pesu koskee vain niiden kiinteistöjen keräysvälineitä, jotka ilmoittautuvat mukaan pesukierrokselle. Perusurakkakausi on 1.4.2027 – 31.3.2029 (2 vuotta), jonka jatkoksi tilaajan ja urakoitsijan on mahdollisuus sopia yhden (1) vuoden optiosopimuksesta.

Company Name, Address, and Unique Entity ID: 2. Point of Contact, Phone number, and Email address: 3. Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Concern (SDVOSBC). d. Veteran Owned Small Business Concern (VOSBC). e. Economically Disadvantaged Woman Owned Small Business Concern (EDWOSB). f. If claiming HUBZone status, provide a copy of your HUBZONE Certificate from the SBA. If claiming SDVOSBC status, provide documentation that shows the Service-Disabled Veteran (SDV) unconditionally owns 51% of the business, controls the management and daily operations, and holds the highest officer position in the company. Documentation should also be provided to show that the SDV has a service-connected disability that has been determined by the Department of Defense or Department of Veteran Affairs. Provide documentation that shows the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. If claiming VOSBC status, provide documentation that shows the Veteran unconditionally owns 51% of the business, controls the management and daily operation, makes long-term decisions for the business, and holds the highest officer position in the company that works at the business fulltime during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. If claiming EDWOSB status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned by one or more women who are "economically disadvantaged", and primarily managed by an economically disadvantaged woman that make long-term decisions for the business, hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full-time during normal working hours. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. A woman is presumed economically disadvantaged if she has a personal net worth of less than $750,000 (with some exclusions), her adjusted gross yearly income averaged over the three years preceding the certification less than $350,000, and the fair market value of all her assets is less than $6 million If claiming Woman Owned Small Business status, provide documentation that shows the company is at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more women, and primarily managed by one or more women that make long-term decisions for the business and hold the highest officer position in the business and work at the business full time during normal working hours. The women must be U.S. citizens. The documentation should also show the business is small under the NAICS code 336611. title: Traumatic Brain Injury and Psychological Health Research Program Public Request for Information
description: The Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) seeks feedback to inform the fiscal year 2027 (FY27) Traumatic Brain Injury and Psychological Health Research Program (TBIPHRP) research focus areas and associated research funding opportunities. Although FY27 federal funds have not yet been appropriated, TBIPRP is collecting this information solely to support strategic program planning. This inquiry does not commit the program to incorporating this feedback into FY27 or any future TBIPHRP funding opportunities. The CDMRP wants to hear from all audiences, interested parties, and individuals from academia, industry, community and non-profit organizations, scientific and professional organizations, federal agencies, and the public. This RFI should not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the TBIPHRP or the Department of War (DoW). BACKGROUND: The CDMRP represents a unique partnership between the U.S. Congress, the military, and the public to fund innovative and impactful medical research in targeted program areas. The CDMRP TBIPHRP�s vision is to optimize the prevention, assessment, and treatment of psychological health conditions and/or traumatic brain injuries. The TBIPHRP�s mission is to fund research to understand, prevent and treat psychological health conditions and/or traumatic brain injuries that accelerates solutions to improve the health and healthcare of Service Members, their Families, Veterans, and the American public. Appropriations for the TBIPHRP from FY21-24 and FY26 totaled $740.5 million. As of October 2026, FY27 funds for the TBIPHRP have not been appropriated. If appropriated, the CDMRP will utilize its two-tier review process https://cdmrp.health.mil/about/2tierRevProcess) to efficiently manage the TBIPHRP. Additional information about the TBIPHRP can be found here: https://cdmrp.health.mil/tbiphrp/ RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Please provide responses to this RFI by clicking on the following link: https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/FY27-TBIPHRP-RFI

title: W023-- Northwoods National Cemetery Office Trailer Lease
description: 1. Subcontracting and Equipment Leasing *** is considering an approach in which we would serve as the prime contractor, managing contract administration, quality assurance, government coordination, and supplier performance. We would engage an established equipment rental company to provide the office trailer, delivery, installation, maintenance, and eventual removal. Would this arrangement be acceptable under the solicitation? Additionally, could you clarify which limitations on subcontracting, if any, would apply to this equipment leasing arrangement? Quoters are strongly encouraged to demonstrate their own relevant experience and capabilities. Reliance on subcontractor experience/ certifications/ licensing to meet these requirements is discouraged and may not be considered sufficient in the evaluation of proposals. Preference will be given to proposals wherein the prime contractor clearly illustrates its direct experience and ability to successfully perform the required work without significant dependence on subcontractor s past performance. FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on subcontracting applies and will be added to awarded contract. 2. Set-Aside and Evaluation Structure The solicitation identifies a total small-business set-aside and establishes a tiered evaluation beginning with SDVOSBs. Can you confirm that SBA-certified SDVOSBs will receive first consideration under the stated evaluation process? Tiered Evaluation The Government will evaluate quotations using a tiered comparative analysis approach. Quotations will first be considered within the highest priority socioeconomic tier identified in this solicitation. Within that tier, the Government will evaluate technical acceptability, past performance, and price in accordance with the stated evaluation criteria and will make a comparative assessment to determine whether award can be made at that level. If award cannot be made within that tier, the Government may proceed to the next tier and repeat the process. This approach preserves the tiered evaluation structure while allowing the Government to compare quotations within the applicable tier to determine the quotation that represents the best value. If the Government is unable to make an award after evaluating all applicable tiers, the Government reserves the right to cancel the solicitation, amend the solicitation, or resolicit as action determined to be in the best interest of the Government. This requirement will be evaluated using a tiered approach in accordance with VAAR 815.101-370 SDVOSB concerns VOSB concerns Small Business concerns (HUBZone, 8(a), EDWOSB, and WOSB) Other Small Business concerns that are not otherwise included in the above categories 3. Past Performance Requirements Volume III requests three comparable past performance references but permits offerors with fewer references to explain their available experience. As a newly established SDVOSB, *** does not yet have three comparable contracts performed under its own name. Would relevant experience from our proposed equipment supplier be considered alongside ***'s management experience, provided we clearly identify each party's role? Quoters are strongly encouraged to demonstrate their own relevant experience and capabilities. Reliance on subcontractor experience/ certifications/ licensing to meet these requirements is discouraged and may not be considered sufficient in the evaluation of proposals. Preference will be given to proposals wherein the prime contractor clearly illustrates its direct experience and ability to successfully perform the required work without significant dependence on subcontractor s past performance. 4. Period of Performance The solicitation identifies an anticipated performance period of January 1 through December 31, 2027, while the pricing schedule references December 14, 2026 through December 13, 2027. Could you confirm the intended period of performance and whether the 30-day delivery requirement begins upon issuance of the Notice to Proceed? The anticipated Period of performance is 1/1/202-13/31/2027, however it may change pending installation of electrical. The Contractor shall provide a temporary office Trailer/Structure within 30 days of NTP (Notice to proceed) for a period of 12 months as well as all transportation, labor, parts, and materials to deliver, setup, secure, dismantle and remove at the end of the lease.

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) - MULTI-CHANNEL MANPACK (MCMP) RADIO CAPABILITY
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) MULTI-CHANNEL MANPACK (MCMP) RADIO CAPABILITY M67854-27-I-2001 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION Document Type: Request for Information/Market Research Sources Sought: All Businesses � Under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 334220 Closing date for RFI: 11 December 2026 at 1600 PM EST This RFI is for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation for bids or proposals and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. No Statement of Work or Performance Specifications is currently available for release. The technical requirements package for this RFI is contained in the Controlled Attachment titled "MCMP System Requirements," which contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). Access to this attachment is restricted and must be requested separately on SAM.gov in accordance with the procedures outlined in Section 4.0. This RFI is a market research tool to determine the availability and adequacy of potential commercial sources. The Government is not obligated to reimburse, and will not pay, for any information received from potential sources as a result of this RFI. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for, or award, a competitive or sole source contract. 2.0 DESCRIPTION The Portfolio Acquisition Executive � Marine Corps (PAE-MC) Program Manager Tactical Communications and Electromagnetic Warfare Systems (PM TCE), Product Manager Tactical Radios (PdM TR), Ground Radios (GR) team is seeking industry feedback regarding a Multi-Channel ManPack (MCMP) Radio capability. The Marine Corps seeks Commercial or Non-Developmental Items (NDI) that can meet Marine Corps operational requirements. The purpose of this RFI is to aid in the requirements generation process and to seek feedback from industry on the status of potential replacements. This RFI is being issued to all available and qualifying vendors to collect information regarding industry capabilities to provide all listed items as an entire system. 3.0 BACKGROUND The Marine Corps seeks a Commercial or NDI solution that meets National Security Agency (NSA) High-Assurance Communications Security (COMSEC) modernization requirements and possesses improved size, weight, and power (SWaP) attributes. The MCMP will be configured in both a mounted (track and wheeled vehicles) and dismounted configuration. Radios will be networkable, enabling command and control at the lowest tactical level. The MCMP will leverage commercially available or non-developmental solutions to rapidly meet operational requirements. However,the Government is primarily interested in technologies currently exhibiting a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 8 or greater to support rapid fielding timelines. 4.0 ACCESS TO CUI ATTACHMENTS (MCMP SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS) The technical specifications outlining the mandatory system capabilities for this effort are contained in the Controlled Attachment titled "MCMP System Requirements". This file contains Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and/or Federal Contract Information (FCI). In accordance with federal security regulations and Department of War (DoW) information security policies, this document is locked to the public on SAM.gov. Interested parties must request access to this document separately on SAM.gov and satisfy the security requirements detailed below. MANDATORY SAM.GOV ACCOUNT SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS Before submitting an access request, your organization must ensure your SAM.gov account is configured correctly: Required Account Roles: The individual user submitting the access request on SAM.gov MUST have been assigned either the "Administrator" or "Data Entry" role in the Contract Opportunities domain for your registered entity. Troubleshooting: If you do not have one of these two roles assigned to your profile, the "Request Access" button will be inactive. The Government contracting office cannot manage, assign, or edit user roles within your company's SAM.gov profile. Please contact your company's internal SAM.gov Entity Administrator to update your permissions. MANDATORY SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS To receive approval to view the "MCMP System Requirements" attachment, vendors must satisfy all of the following requirements: Active SAM.gov Registration: The entity's registration must be active and complete. Executed Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA): A signed copy of the Government-furnished "MCMP Project Non-Disclosure Agreement" (attached publicly to this announcement as Attachment 1). And one of the following: Active DD Form 2345 (JCP): Your company must hold an approved DD Form 2345 with the Joint Certification Program (JCP) through the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA). SPRS NIST SP 800-171 Score: A current self-assessment score must be posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level 2: A current CMMC Level 2 self-assessment or CMMC third-party assessment. INSTRUCTIONS TO REQUEST ACCESS To request access to the "MCMP System Requirements" attachment: Log into SAM.gov with your credentialed account, navigate to this opportunity notice, locate the "MCMP System Requirements" attachment, and click "Request Access." In the justification text box provided by SAM.gov, you MUST input your company's Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI). Requests lacking a CAGE code will be rejected. Download Attachment 1 (MCMP Project Non-Disclosure Agreement) from the public attachments section of this notice. Complete, sign, and date the agreement. Send a companion verification email to Hyung Lee, hyung.lee@usmc.mil, with a courtesy copy to Wanda Harner, wanda.harner@usmc.mil. Use the subject line: `MCMP RFI CUI Access Request - [Company Name] - CAGE: [XXXXX]`. Attach to the email: (1) Your executed MCMP Project NDA, AND (2) ONE of the following verifying documents: A copy of your active DD Form 2345 (JCP), OR Proof/screenshot of your posted SPRS score, OR Proof of your current CMMC Level 2 certification. 5.0 RESPONSE FORMAT Responses should be prepared in accordance with the following guidelines: Utilizing either Word (docx, 2013 or newer) or Adobe (.pdf) software. Times New Roman 12 (or larger) font, single-spaced, including tables, on 8.5 by 11 inches paper. A font size smaller than 12 may be used in figures and drawings, but type shall be clearly legible. Margins on all sides (top, bottom, left, and right) shall be at least 1 inch. A cover sheet that includes: Project title. Company name. Product name(s) Primary point of contact, including name, address, phone and e-mail contact information; and Date of submission. Interested parties are requested to provide an information package addressing their approach to meeting the Mandatory Requirements listed above, to include the following: Your organization�s description of, and its capability to provide, an integrated solution which meets the requirements defined in this RFI. Please provide details concerning integration efforts as well as components to be used. A description of your device specifications addressing each functional area under the mandatory system requirements. The technological readiness levels of all components used, and an assessment of when production models can be delivered. If additional testing is required, a detailed assessment of how long it would take to meet testing requirements following contract award. A detailed assessment and recommendation on any capability, which if relief were granted or deferred, could accelerate fielding of a multi-channel manpack radio capability. How any additional features of the system noted in your response meet or exceed the objective requirements. Known or expected production and delivery timelines and supply chain constraints. Whether your solution is considered commercially available off-the shelf or a non-developmental item in accordance with FAR 2.1
